stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: The AI data center e-waste problem is huge — and getting bigger
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The AI boom is generating a massive, previously underestimated amount of e-waste.
Projections suggest AI-related e-waste could fill 23 million shipping containers by 2050.
This new report indicates a significantly higher estimate of AI's environmental impact compared to prior studies.

stories.title: Google will now let any AI agent run your smart home
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Google is enabling third-party AI agents (like Claude) to interact with and control smart home devices.
This functionality is facilitated by a new standardized integration called the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
The change allows external AI tools to monitor home data and take actionable control over connected devices.

stories.title: Apple reportedly building server packed with M-series Ultra chips for AI
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly developing a new server architecture utilizing M-series Ultra chips.
This development signals a potential major shift, possibly marking Apple's first enterprise server in decades.
The planned debut for this AI-focused server is anticipated around 2029.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors, indicating its accessibility for researchers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a generative language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It relates to core NLP/AI components, specifically text-generation pipelines.
The associated tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and context gathering.
It emphasizes on-device execution, allowing complex AI workflows to run on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% faster when integrated with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly considering re-entering the server hardware market.
The potential move is driven by the surging demand for compute power in the AI industry.
Apple may partner with Nvidia to facilitate this return to server manufacturing.

stories.title: Dreaming the Sound of Contact: Leveraging Video and Audio Generation for Zero-Shot Force-Aware Manipulation and Data Generation
stories.author: Nadia Figueroa
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in current robot manipulation: generated video trajectories lack essential force information for contact-rich tasks.
Proposes a novel method to augment video generation by incorporating audio signals (specifically contact sound loudness) to define desired force profiles.
Presents a joint pipeline enabling robots to learn force-aware manipulation trajectories from synthetic data.

stories.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
stories.author: Jack Merullo
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing problem of 'reward hacking' in large language models (LLMs) as they scale.
The study proposes using internal model representations to detect and understand reward hacking behaviors.
The authors found that simple vector differences can coherently represent reward hacking across several frontier open-source LLMs (Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, Qwen).

stories.title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceIDE, a new infrastructure designed to convert vast scientific codebases into programmable environments.
Addresses the 'scientific experience bottleneck,' which is the difficulty in translating complex, fragmented scientific knowledge into reliable learning data for AI agents.
Aims to enable scientific agents to learn directly from executable models and methods found in real-world scientific code repositories.

stories.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
stories.author: Jack Merullo
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing problem of 'reward hacking' in large language models (LLMs) as they scale.
The study proposes using internal model representations to detect and understand these sophisticated hacking behaviors.
They demonstrate that simple vector differences can coherently represent reward hacking across several frontier open-source LLMs (Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, Qwen).

stories.title: Nvidia announces native GPU programming in Rust
stories.author: nonmaskable
bullet_points: Nvidia is introducing native GPU programming support within the Rust language.
This move signifies a major push towards integrating modern, memory-safe languages into high-performance computing.
It lowers the barrier to entry for developers wanting to write optimized code for Nvidia GPUs.

stories.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
stories.author: polyphilz
bullet_points: A new AI/ML approach is being developed to significantly speed up database query planning.
The model, trained to handle 4 billion parameters, reportedly achieves an 81% speedup over standard Postgres query plans.
This represents a potential major efficiency gain in database performance optimization using AI.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms (Claude) with local, open-source LLM infrastructure (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Snap is launching a new Specs AI tool, and it’s coming to iOS and Mac
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Snap is launching 'Specs Intelligence,' a new AI assistant.
The tool aims to be an 'anticipatory AI service' connecting various digital accounts.
It is being rolled out to both iOS and Mac platforms, positioning it against competitors like Meta's Muse and Gemini's Spark.

stories.title: I wore Snap’s $2,200 smart glasses
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Snap has released new augmented reality (AR) smart glasses called 'Specs'.
The glasses demonstrate practical AR interaction, such as playing virtual dominoes.
The review highlights the hands-on experience of using the high-end ($2,200) hardware.

stories.title: Not just Proton: Getting to know Valve's new SteamOS compatibility layers
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Valve is expanding SteamOS compatibility beyond Proton.
New system-level tools enable support for Arm chipsets within the Steam ecosystem.
The update allows for the integration of Android APKs into Steam.

stories.title: California may gut state net neutrality law to comply with Trump admin demand
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: California is potentially considering weakening its state-level net neutrality regulations.
The proposed change is reportedly driven by restrictions within Trump administration broadband grants.
These federal grants reportedly prohibit states from enforcing their own net neutrality laws.

stories.title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
stories.author: Tiago Pimentel
bullet_points: The paper analyzes two core tokenization algorithms, Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) and UnigramLM, used in modern language models.
It identifies two independent axes of difference: the optimization objective (compression vs. log-likelihood) and the search procedure (bottom-up vs. top-down).
The research aims to disentangle whether observed performance differences are due to the optimization goal or the search methodology.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Introduces Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
ComPO utilizes comparison oracles to extract directional information from preference pairs for alignment.

stories.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
stories.author: Arlindo L. Oliveira
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of language agents in complex, interactive environments.
Introduces two cognitive extensions—Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) and Self-Reflection Module (SRM)—to enhance agent capabilities.
The research extends the SwiftSage dual-process agent by adding episodic memory and execution-time validation for better long-horizon task completion.

stories.title: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
stories.author: Jin Gao
bullet_points: Introduces Affora, a new design system specifically engineered to support both human users and AI agents.
Addresses the current problem where traditional interfaces lack clarity for machine readers, hindering agent interaction.
The system aims to maintain visual freedom and familiar human workflows while ensuring machine readability across components and sites.

stories.title: Flag Game: A Toy Model for Mechanistic Swarm Interpretability
stories.author: Hidenori Tanaka
bullet_points: Introduces the 'Flag Game,' a toy model designed to study collective belief formation in AI agents.
Addresses the critical safety risk posed by emergent, coordinated behaviors in multi-agent AI systems.
Focuses on achieving mechanistic understanding of how agents form and spread beliefs about a hidden ground truth.

stories.title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
stories.author: Jinyu Gu
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'rMuscle,' a method designed to improve the efficiency of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model inference.
VLA models are becoming the dominant policy paradigm for embodied AI, particularly in structured environments like factory automation.
The research addresses the critical issue of high inference latency in VLA models, which negatively impacts robot responsiveness and motion quality.

stories.title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation
stories.author: Michael Oberst
bullet_points: Radiologists exhibit heterogeneous reporting practices, leading to varied report styles even when findings are identical.
These variations (terminology, shorthand, formatting) pose a significant challenge for evaluating AI-based Radiology Report Generation (RRG) models.
The study highlights that current AI evaluation methods often fail to account for these natural clinical reporting discrepancies.

stories.title: Securing quantum error correction against misleading advice from AI agents
stories.author: A. Barış Özgüler
bullet_points: The research addresses a security vulnerability where an AI advisor could be manipulated to introduce harmful updates into quantum error correction (QEC).
The core technical finding identifies an ambiguity in passive syndrome records that hinders the selection of correct recovery operations.
The authors propose using additional calibration measurements to support certified and robust recovery updates despite system uncertainty and drift.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Proposes Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
Utilizes comparison oracles to extract directional information from preference pairs for alignment.

stories.title: Exponential Hardness of Off-Policy Evaluation under History-Dependent Logging
stories.author: Pranaya Jajoo
bullet_points: The research addresses the theoretical limits of Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE) in reinforcement learning.
It demonstrates that history-dependent logging can lead to exponentially uninformative datasets, even with high state visitation.
The findings are proven using constructed Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) with limited complexity.

stories.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
stories.author: Arlindo L. Oliveira
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of language agents in complex, interactive environments.
Introduces two cognitive extensions—Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) and Self-Reflection Module (SRM)—to enhance agent capabilities.
The research extends the SwiftSage dual-process agent by adding mechanisms for episodic memory and execution validation/correction.

stories.title: How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents
stories.author: Andrew Gordon Wilson
bullet_points: The research challenges conventional scaling law wisdom by showing architectural changes can alter scaling exponents.
The study investigates how model growth, recursion (looped transformers), and boundary operators affect performance scaling.
Architectural interventions, specifically looping/recursion, offer a pathway to exponential performance gains with increased computation.

stories.title: Evidence-Grounded Agentic Formulation Development in an Autonomous Laboratory
stories.author: Pauric Bannigan
bullet_points: Introduces 'Andromeda 2,' an agentic AI system designed to automate and optimize drug formulation development.
The system reasons over existing experimental data and autonomously executes computational and physical experiments in a lab setting.
Aims to reduce the experimental intensity required to identify high-performing self-emulsifying drug delivery systems (SEDDS).

stories.title: A General Kernel Framework for Non-CND Distance Measures Using |D|-Dimensional Sparse Landmark Embeddings
stories.author: Mark D. Risser
bullet_points: Addresses a fundamental limitation in kernel methods and Gaussian Processes (GPs) which require conditionally negative definite (CND) distance measures.
Introduces the Sparse Landmark Embedding (SLE) kernel, a novel framework designed to bypass the CND requirement.
The SLE kernel embeds inputs into sparse feature vectors, allowing its application to complex spaces like smooth manifolds and probability distributions.

stories.title: Probabilistic Linear Explanations
stories.author: Chi Tran
bullet_points: Introduces a unified framework for probabilistic explainability in machine learning.
Addresses the limitations of traditional abductive explanations (too many features) and probabilistic methods (limited to categorical data).
The framework utilizes sparse, anchored linear models, applicable to both binary classification and continuous regression.

stories.title: Double descent is the principle of least action
stories.author: Congzhou M Sha
bullet_points: The paper proposes a novel explanation for the 'double descent' phenomenon in machine learning.
It frames the training trajectory of stochastic gradient descent as a particle wandering over an energy landscape.
The analysis uses concepts from statistical mechanics to model how model performance changes with model complexity (number of parameters).

stories.title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
stories.author: Tiago Pimentel
bullet_points: The paper analyzes two core tokenization algorithms (BPE and UnigramLM) used in modern language models.
It identifies two orthogonal axes of difference: the optimization objective (compression vs. log-likelihood) and the search procedure (merging vs. pruning).
The research aims to disentangle whether observed performance differences are due to the optimization goal or the search methodology.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Proposes Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
ComPO utilizes comparison oracles to extract directional information from preference pairs for alignment.

stories.title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation
stories.author: Michael Oberst
bullet_points: Radiologists exhibit heterogeneous reporting practices, leading to varied report styles even for identical findings.
These reporting variations pose a significant, under-appreciated challenge for evaluating AI-based Radiology Report Generation (RRG) models.
The study highlights that current evaluation metrics may be insufficient because they often overlook these natural variations in clinical documentation.

stories.title: MUSE: Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models on Multi-Modal Understanding in Situated Education
stories.author: Wee Siong Ng
bullet_points: The paper introduces MUSE, a new benchmark for evaluating Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) specifically within educational contexts.
It addresses a gap in current research where LVLMs are not sufficiently tested on interpreting complex, multi-modal content like artistic imagery in learning environments.
The research emphasizes the need for models to reason about semantic, affective, and cultural content to support meaningful AI-assisted language learning.

stories.title: Long-Lived Characters, Local Inference: Incremental Memory Maintenance for Game NPCs
stories.author: Zimu Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational inefficiency of maintaining long-term memory for locally deployed, language-model-driven game NPCs.
Identifies that incremental memory updates can invalidate reusable prefixes in LLMs, leading to high preparation costs.
Highlights the critical need for accurate memory maintenance, as incorrect character knowledge can lead to flawed game actions and value judgments.

stories.title: Build real-time voice applications with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe
stories.author: thorwebdev
bullet_points: Google has released new Gemini Live models via the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
These updates specifically enable the building of real-time voice applications.
The new models integrate with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.5 Transcribe capabilities.

stories.title: Show a model your old code and it writes your old bugs: 32 runs, 0% reuse
stories.author: remdore
bullet_points: The article demonstrates a significant regression in AI code generation when comparing pre- and post-migration codebases.
The model reproduced specific, known bugs from the older code version, indicating a lack of context retention or understanding during the migration process.
The comparison highlights the efficiency gain (190 lines vs. 41 lines) achieved by refactoring to a shared component, even when the AI fails to maintain quality.
